nodes.binding: Assess DVD identity for the specific object tracked from the source image using shape, location, and surrounding context. Do not infer identity solely because an edited object is a white disc; report uncertainty if the source object cannot confidently be identified or matched.

program.checker_template: Evaluate ONE independent required condition against the SOURCE and EDITED images. No reference label, previous answers or optimization feedback is supplied. Return pass if the condition is satisfied, fail if it is not satisfied, or unknown if the evidence cannot establish an answer. Inspect only this saved condition, its criteria and binding. Report factual evidence and confidence (0..1 or null). A pass means satisfaction of THIS condition, not an overall edit label. Do not anticipate the optimizer's target. Missing evidence or transport/schema failures must not become a negative observation. The final overall label is computed by code; you never supply it.

d2: The binding over-focuses on whether the source item is independently recognizable as a DVD and explicitly directs uncertainty when identity is not confident. In the images, the small rectangular item near the center is replaced by a white disc at roughly the same location, while another white disc is on the dark object to the right; the source item’s DVD identity and which edited disc corresponds to it are not established. This is genuine visual ambiguity, not a transport, schema, or dependency failure. Keep the identity/correspondence check, but make its evidence procedure distinguish the candidate discs using location, shape, and scene context, and separate “the requested edit visibly progressed” from “the same source object remains identifiable as a DVD.” The rubric’s aggregate label is no, but it is not atomic ground truth for this identity criterion; do not force a fail or infer that no edit occurred from the unresolved trace. The high-confidence unknown and zero coverage indicate the criterion/binding may be routing an aggregate progress judgment through an identity-only check. Clarify that this node should return only the identity judgment, leaving requested-change progress to the appropriate criterion, and reserve unknown for cases where correspondence or identity truly cannot be resolved.
d1: The binding already asks for source-to-edited correspondence, but its instruction to report unknown whenever correspondence is ambiguous may make the node stop at uncertainty instead of evaluating the visible evidence. Keep the identity check, and direct the node to compare the source item’s position and surrounding scene with each edited candidate, weighing location alongside shape and context rather than requiring the DVD to remain independently recognizable. Here, the source shows a small rectangular item near the center; the edit shows a white disc near that location and another on the dark object to the right. The trace should assess these candidates explicitly, without assuming either is the same DVD or treating a new white disc as proof of recoloring. Keep identity/correspondence separate from whether any requested change visibly progressed, so this node returns only its identity judgment and the aggregate criterion can assess progress elsewhere. Reserve unknown for genuinely unresolved correspondence; do not force a fail from the aggregate “no” label. This is a semantic/routing issue, not a transport, schema, or dependency failure.
